content:
If you've been testing Apple Watch beta apps all summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has confirmed the issue and is now automatically updating these apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The updates are being pushed through the App Store, with release notes stating: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features were introduced."

Apple notified developers earlier this week, saying the entire update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems, is expected to roll out to the public around mid-September, so these necessary updates should just make it in before launch.

Apple explained that because some watchOS apps are experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture, this measure is necessary. Reports indicate the company is automatically reprocessing and repackaging affected apps to fix binary compatibility problems, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers having to do anything extra.
